Public infrastructure fails publicly — the architecture has to assume it

Smart infrastructure is IoT at civic scale: water networks, district energy, traffic, public buildings. The stakes shift — service continuity is a public duty, SCADA safety is non-negotiable, and public data carries privacy expectations that private fleets never meet. The engineering keeps the domain's disciplines and adds segmentation: IT/OT boundaries that are real, monitored and drill-tested.

The practice covers the instrumentation census, the segmented architecture (Purdue-style zones with controlled crossings), continuity SLOs per service, and the analytics tier where optimization happens safely behind the boundary.
Below: the failure modes that make infrastructure programs fragile, the reference architecture of segmented continuity, and the console that keeps continuity honest.
Four failure modes that make infrastructure programs fragile
Each of these turns a modernization into a headline — the countermeasures segment the estate, sign continuity SLOs and govern what the public can see.

blocks.x: Reference architecture — segmented, SCADA-safe, SLO'd

IT and OT are segmented by design with controlled crossings, service continuity carries signed SLOs per utility, public-facing data passes through a governed exposure layer, and vendor islands integrate through normalization contracts — so the operating picture is one, and the failures stay small.

nodes.label: BMS & controls
nodes.detail: Vendor systems integrated through normalized ontology models — control authority stays with the BMS; the platform proposes, operators dispose.

nodes.label: Metering fabric
nodes.detail: Circuit-level metering with unit contracts — the M&V baseline is only as honest as the meter data.

nodes.label: Semantic model
nodes.detail: Brick/Haystack-class ontology across 7 system types — analytics read one model, not seven vendor schemas.

nodes.label: Occupancy sensing
nodes.detail: Zone-level occupancy aggregated with privacy by design — no individual tracking, ever; the estate measures rooms, not people.

nodes.label: Energy optimization
nodes.detail: Setpoint scheduling within comfort bands against tariff windows — bounds, operator override and M&V verification built in.

nodes.label: Demand response
nodes.detail: Market participation where allowed — load flexibility bid against comfort constraints, with the control room's override preserved.

nodes.label: Operations console
nodes.detail: One pane for the estate teams — alarms with context, comfort compliance, energy position — the platform serves the operators first.

nodes.label: Privacy governance
nodes.detail: Occupancy data governance with published principles — city-scale platforms survive on the privacy contract, not on the sensors.
